title: Public Sector (Governance) (Amendment) Bill at Second Reading
what_it_is: A Second Reading debate on the Public Sector (Governance) (Amendment) Bill, which would allow public agencies to share data with trusted external partners under safeguards and create related offences for misuse.
why_it_matters: The Minister said the amendments will enable vulnerable Singaporeans to receive faster, targeted and more coordinated support, when they need it most. She also said families in need currently repeat their stories and details to many parties, and the Bill introduces criminal offences for individuals in external organisations who misuse shared data. The record does not set out commencement dates or other practical impacts beyond these stated aims.

key_points.point: The Bill was moved for Second Reading.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: I move, “That the Bill be now read a Second time.”

key_points.point: The PSGA was introduced in 2018 to enable public agencies to share data safely and purposefully.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: It helped to enable, among other objectives, public agencies to share data safely and purposefully, so that we can serve Singaporeans better.

key_points.point: The Bill provides a clear legal basis with guardrails for data sharing with trusted external partners where it serves legitimate public purposes.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: It provides a clear legal basis with guardrails for data sharing with our trusted external partners, where it serves legitimate public purposes.

key_points.point: The Bill sets three safeguards: legitimate purpose, Ministerial or delegate authorisation, and contractual terms of use.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: having a legitimate purpose for sharing; (b) the arrangement is specifically authorised by a Minister or the Minister's delegate; and (c) the external partner is bound by clear contractual terms of use, including data protection and security requirements.

key_points.point: The Bill does not authorise data sharing for commercial exploitation, marketing or unrelated purposes.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: It does not authorise data sharing for commercial exploitation, marketing or unrelated purposes.

key_points.point: Individuals in external organisations face the same penalties as public officers for misusing shared data.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: individuals in external organisations face the same level of penalties that public officers are currently subject to for misusing shared data.

key_points.point: The Bill clarifies that public agencies are permitted to use their own data to work more effectively.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: public agencies are permitted to use their own data to work more effectively.

key_points.point: The PSGA and the forthcoming Health Information Bill are complementary.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: Both the PSGA and the HIB are complementary Bills.

key_points.point: The MDDI Government Parliamentary Committee and PAP MPs support the Bill.
key_points.speaker: Mr Sharael Taha
key_points.quote: the MPs of the Ministry of Digital Development and Information (MDDI) Government Parliamentary Committee (GPC) stand in support of this important Bill.

key_points.point: Ms He Ting Ru said the shift to executive discretion should be founded in necessity.
key_points.speaker: Ms He Ting Ru
key_points.quote: Such a shift from a more rule-based model of data governance to one that relies more heavily on executive decision and ultimately, discretion, should be founded in necessity.

key_points.point: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo said the offences carry fines of up to $5,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jessica Tan Soon Neo
key_points.quote: These offences carry the same penalties already set out in the PSGA, which are fines of up to $5,000, imprisonment of up to two years, or both.

key_points.point: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat asked for a public register of data sharing directions issued to private entities.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
key_points.quote: All data sharing directions issued to private entities should be published – the categories of data shared, the recipient, the purpose, the duration.

key_points.point: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat asked for a formal public review within five years.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
key_points.quote: would the Minister commit to a formal public review within five years, including the directions issued, the data shared and whether the safeguards have been adequate?

key_points.point: Dr Choo Pei Ling proposed a public register of health data shared under PSGA for non-health purposes.
key_points.speaker: Dr Choo Pei Ling
key_points.quote: I propose that the Government jointly maintain a public register of all use cases where health data has been shared under PSGA for non-health purposes.

key_points.point: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry said data sharing must not be driven by convenience.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kwek Hian Chuan Henry
key_points.quote: data sharing must not be driven by convenience. It must be controlled, accountable and safe, especially when we share data with external partners.

key_points.point: Ms Jasmin Lau said there is no shift from a rule-based framework to executive discretion.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: Let me be clear, there is no such shift.

key_points.point: Ms Jasmin Lau said existing PSGA purposes and data governance rules remain fully in place.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: The existing PSGA stipulates seven purposes under which a Ministerial direction may be made for data sharing these clear purposes, as well as all existing data governance rules remain fully in place.

key_points.point: Ms Jasmin Lau said Terms of Use will include anti-malware software and regular vulnerability assessments.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: These Terms of Use will include data security and protection safeguards, such as using anti-malware software with up-to-date signatures and performing regular vulnerability assessments.

key_points.point: Ms Jasmin Lau said allowing individuals to opt out would lead to incomplete data and undermine planning and service delivery.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: Allowing individuals to opt out would lead to incomplete data, which will fundamentally undermine our ability to plan, formulate policies and deliver services.

key_points.point: Ms Jasmin Lau said the Government will consider what is practical on a list of external partners.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: We will consider what is practical.

key_points.point: Ms Jasmin Lau said the Government came to Parliament and clarified the legal framework when the TraceTogether issue arose.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: When the issue arose, the Government came to Parliament, explained the position and clarified the legal framework.

key_points.point: Ms Jasmin Lau said organisational liability for external partners is contractual.
key_points.speaker: Ms Jasmin Lau
key_points.quote: On the first question, contractual liabilities.

key_points.point: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat asked whether liability is contractual or statutory.
key_points.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
key_points.quote: Is it contractual liability or statutory liability?

not_said: Whether a public register of data sharing directions issued to private entities will be published.
Whether a formal public review within five years will be committed to.
Whether organisational statutory liability for non-personal data will be introduced.
How many times agencies encountered difficulties providing services in the last five years.
Whether a public register of health data shared under PSGA for non-health purposes will be maintained.
Whether targeted funding or capability-building programmes will be provided to smaller external partners.
Whether common frameworks, grants, training or shared platforms will be provided to help partners meet requirements.
Whether annual reports on health information requests for employment or insurance purposes will be published.
